# Shared protocol conformance corpus.
#
# Gate C requires that "a host simulator or protocol fixture and the firmware
# agree on framing and versions". This file is that agreement, written down.
# Two independent implementations of the same draft agree right up until they do
# not; a corpus both must reproduce is what turns that into a test failure
# instead of a bring-up surprise.
#
# Consumed by:
#   - pycontrol/tests/test_fixture_corpus.py   (the Python simulator)
#   - test/native/test_protocol/test_protocol.cpp             (the RP2040 half)
#
# BOTH consumers exist as of 2026-09-03, which is when this file started being
# evidence rather than a restatement of one implementation. Change a case and
# BOTH must be re-run: `pixi run pycontrol-test` and `pixi run -- pio test -e
# native`. A change that only one side is checked against silently forks the
# contract.
#
# Format is line-oriented, not JSON, so the C++ side can parse it with getline
# and a prefix compare rather than pulling in a JSON library. It is also
# diffable and greppable, which is the same rule the protocol itself follows.
#
#   CASE <name>       begin a case; the board is freshly booted, READY drained,
#                     clock at 0, serial 0000000000000000, defaults otherwise
#   SEND <line>       feed one command line (the \n is implied)
#   ADVANCE <us>      advance simulated time by <us> microseconds
#   ANGLE <deg>       the animal moves the joystick: the encoder reads <deg>
#                     from now on, with no driver involvement, and the board
#                     services once at the current time so the classifier sees
#                     the sample. Added 2026-10-01 for the WATCH outcomes; the
#                     stimulus takes effect in any state (the simulator and the
#                     firmware's simulated backend simply set the encoder), but
#                     only RELEASED gives it a meaning.
#   TORQUE <Ncm>      reserved for the torque stimulus; no case uses it until a
#                     board reports `torque` in its caps.
#   EXPECT <line>     the next output line, in order
#   END               end of case; no further output may be pending
#
# Every EXPECT is exact bytes. Blank lines and # lines are ignored.
#
# Board defaults these cases assume, from BoardSim's constructor:
#   serial 0000000000000000   fw 0.0.0   hw rev0   proto 2   axes 1
#   travel -20.0..20.0 deg    v_max 180.0 deg/s    home takes 50000 us
#   host timeout 100000 us    home timeout maximum 8000000 us
#   caps motion+home+instr+hv+watch+fetch+stream+cfg (no brake, torque, angout)
#   deadband 0.5 deg          stream_hz 10          instrumentation on at boot
#   pull direction = +angle   capture ring 1 kHz from RELEASED; pre_ms 500, post_ms 500
#
# Timestamps and durations are exact: `t` is the board's 64-bit microsecond
# clock, and every deadline (watchdog, home bound, hold, timeout, maxdur, the
# one-second TRIAL rule, stream and capture samples) is stepped to exactly, so
# an event lands on the microsecond its rule names.
#
# Move distances here are chosen to divide evenly at v_max (9 deg = 50000 us) so
# no case depends on how a duration is rounded. The firmware and the simulator
# both truncate, but that is not something a corpus should be pinning by
# accident - if rounding ever matters, it needs a case that says so on purpose.


# --------------------------------------------------------------- versions

# The one case that must never be allowed to drift silently: a peer reads the
# protocol version and axis count from here and refuses a mismatch rather than
# guessing. The axis count is also what distinguishes this board from the
# twin-axis board on the same link.
CASE id-reports-version-serial-and-axis-count
  SEND id;1
  EXPECT ack;1;hw=rev0;serial=0000000000000000;fw=0.0.0;proto=2;axes=1;caps=motion+home+instr+hv+watch+fetch+stream+cfg;rxbuf=200
END

# "Must work before ARM and must never fail" - including before HV is on.
CASE id-answers-before-arm
  SEND id;7
  EXPECT ack;7;hw=rev0;serial=0000000000000000;fw=0.0.0;proto=2;axes=1;caps=motion+home+instr+hv+watch+fetch+stream+cfg;rxbuf=200
END


# ------------------------------------------------ the draft's own examples

# `cal;419;get -> ack;419;enc_offset=1024;angle_zero=0.0`
CASE draft-example-cal-get
  SEND cal;419;get
  EXPECT ack;419;enc_offset=1024;angle_zero=0.0
END

# `movetoo;420;-12.5 -> nak;420;badverb`
CASE draft-example-unknown-verb
  SEND movetoo;420;-12.5
  EXPECT nak;420;badverb
END

# `moveto;421;-999 -> nak;421;outofrange`
#
# The draft shows this reply without saying which state the board was in, and
# ordering matters: this implementation checks ARMED *before* range, so from a
# fresh board the same line answers `notarmed`. Reproducing the draft's example
# therefore requires an armed board, which is what this case sets up. The
# ordering choice is deliberate - refusing motion outside ARMED is the
# safety-relevant rule and should not be reachable past an argument check.
CASE draft-example-out-of-range-when-armed
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND moveto;421;-999
  EXPECT nak;421;outofrange
END


# ------------------------------------------------------ framing robustness

CASE bad-frame-without-a-sequence-number
  SEND ping
  EXPECT nak;?;badframe
END

CASE bad-frame-with-an-unreadable-sequence-number
  SEND ping;notanumber
  EXPECT nak;?;badframe
END

CASE empty-field-is-a-bad-frame
  SEND ;
  EXPECT nak;?;badframe
END

# Verbs decode case-insensitively; the draft's table is uppercase and its
# examples are lowercase.
CASE verbs-are-case-insensitive
  SEND PING;3
  EXPECT ack;3
END

# A CRLF peer leaves a carriage return before the newline.
CASE carriage-return-is-tolerated
  SEND ping;4\r
  EXPECT ack;4
END

# A repeated seq with identical content is re-acknowledged, byte for byte.
CASE retransmission-is-reacknowledged-identically
  SEND cal;9;set;enc_offset;2048
  EXPECT ack;9;enc_offset=2048
  SEND cal;9;set;enc_offset;2048
  EXPECT ack;9;enc_offset=2048
END


# ------------------------------------------------------- state machine gates

CASE motion-is-refused-outside-armed
  SEND moveto;1;5.0
  EXPECT nak;1;notarmed
END

# The ordering above is pinned deliberately: ARMED is checked BEFORE the range
# check, so an OUT-OF-RANGE value from an UNARMED board answers `notarmed` and
# not `outofrange`. Refusing motion outside ARMED is the safety-relevant rule
# and must not be reachable past an argument check.
#
# `motion-is-refused-outside-armed` above cannot pin this, because 5.0 is in
# range and both orderings answer `notarmed`. Only an out-of-range value from an
# unarmed board tells the two apart. Added 2026-09-03 after mutation-testing the
# corpus against the firmware: inverting the two checks passed every case in
# this file, which meant the corpus documented an ordering it did not enforce.
CASE armed-is-checked-before-the-range-check
  SEND moveto;1;-999
  EXPECT nak;1;notarmed
END

CASE homing-requires-the-motor-rail
  SEND home;1
  EXPECT nak;1;nohv
END

CASE arm-is-refused-before-homing
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND arm;2
  EXPECT nak;2;nothomed
END

# The full path from boot to a completed move, which is the sequence a task
# actually performs.
CASE arm-then-move-to-completion
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND moveto;4;9.0
  EXPECT ack;4
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;TARGET;100000;angle=9.0
END

# Heartbeat loss faults the board without host cooperation, drops HV_EN, and is
# reported as fault bit 0.
CASE heartbeat-loss-faults-the-board
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 100000
  EXPECT ev;FAULT;150000;code=0;detail=host_timeout
  SEND status;4
  EXPECT ack;4;state=FAULTED;angle=0.0;xactual=0.0;torque=;brake=;homed=1;limit=0;faults=1;hv=0;t=150000
END


# ------------------------------------------------------------- observability

CASE status-is-safe-before-anything-is-configured
  SEND status;1
  EXPECT ack;1;state=IDLE;angle=0.0;xactual=0.0;torque=;brake=;homed=0;limit=0;faults=0;hv=0;t=0
END

CASE limits-reports-what-the-board-will-enforce
  SEND limits;1
  EXPECT ack;1;travel_lo=-20.0;travel_hi=20.0;v_max=180.0;a_max=3600.0;i_max=0.421
END

CASE hv-state-is-observable-not-inferred
  SEND hv;1;state
  EXPECT ack;1;hv=0
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND hv;3;state
  EXPECT ack;3;hv=1
END


# ------------------------------------------------------------- compliance

# The trial shape the rig needs: park, present, then let the animal move the
# joystick. `BRAKE <torque>` is the one verb for "engage the brake, then release
# the drive"; on a board whose caps lack `brake` it is accepted, the torque is
# ignored and only the release happens. It replaced `FREEWHEEL` on 2026-10-01.
# The ack comes first and RELEASED when the release has happened.
CASE brake-releases-the-driver
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND brake;4;0
  EXPECT ack;4
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND status;5
  EXPECT ack;5;state=RELEASED;angle=0.0;xactual=0.0;torque=;brake=;homed=1;limit=0;faults=0;hv=1;t=50000
END

# Release is only reachable from ARMED. A joystick held by an energised motor
# cannot go compliant by accident.
CASE brake-is-refused-before-arming
  SEND brake;1;0
  EXPECT nak;1;notarmed
END

CASE brake-needs-a-torque-argument
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND brake;4
  EXPECT nak;4;badargs
END

# The two bring-up verbs are gone, not aliased.
CASE freewheel-and-armpull-are-no-longer-verbs
  SEND freewheel;1
  EXPECT nak;1;badverb
  SEND armpull;2;5.0
  EXPECT nak;2;badverb
END

# Moving to a bounded position is what presents the joystick to the animal.
CASE move-to-the-pull-position
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND moveto;4;-9.0
  EXPECT ack;4
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;TARGET;100000;angle=-9.0
END


# ------------------------------------------------------ 2026-10-01 review

# `t` is the board's 64-bit microsecond clock. 2^32 us is 71.6 minutes, inside
# a normal session; the firmware used to wrap there.
CASE event-time-is-64-bit
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  ADVANCE 4294967296
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;4295017296;angle=0.0
END

# `home;<s>;<timeout_ms>` is a deadline on the running home, not a comparison
# with the expected duration up front (which faulted every request under the
# real backend's 8 s bound immediately).
CASE home-timeout-faults-when-it-expires
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2;30
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 29999
  ADVANCE 1
  EXPECT ev;FAULT;30000;code=3;detail=home_timeout
END

# A timeout above the firmware maximum is clipped to it. With the simulated
# 50 ms home the clip itself is not observable here (both halves pin it in
# their unit tests); what this case pins is that a long bound does not fault a
# home that completed, however far the clock then runs.
CASE home-timeout-above-the-maximum-is-clipped-not-refused
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2;999999
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  ADVANCE 8000000
END

# The board enables the InstrumentPort buffers at boot for its proof of life,
# so STATE reports them on; the verb drives them from then on.
CASE instrumentation-is-on-at-boot
  SEND instr;1;state
  EXPECT ack;1;instr=1
  SEND instr;2;off
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND instr;3;state
  EXPECT ack;3;instr=0
END


# ------------------------------------------------------ configuration (v1)

CASE cfg-reports-and-bounds-its-keys
  SEND cfg;1;get
  EXPECT ack;1;wdt_ms=100;deadband_deg=0.5;stream_hz=10;pre_ms=500;post_ms=500
  SEND cfg;2;wdt_ms=10
  EXPECT nak;2;outofrange
  SEND cfg;3;bogus=1
  EXPECT nak;3;badargs
  SEND cfg;4;wdt_ms=200;deadband_deg=1
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND cfg;5;get
  EXPECT ack;5;wdt_ms=200;deadband_deg=1.0;stream_hz=10;pre_ms=500;post_ms=500
  SEND cfg;6;pre_ms=1500;post_ms=600
  EXPECT nak;6;outofrange
  SEND cfg;7;pre_ms=2047;post_ms=0
  EXPECT ack;7
  SEND cfg;8;post_ms=1
  EXPECT nak;8;outofrange
  SEND cfg;9;get
  EXPECT ack;9;wdt_ms=200;deadband_deg=1.0;stream_hz=10;pre_ms=2047;post_ms=0
END

# A value outside its bounds applies nothing in the line, not even the valid
# pairs before it.
CASE cfg-applies-all-or-nothing
  SEND cfg;1;deadband_deg=2;wdt_ms=9999
  EXPECT nak;1;outofrange
  SEND cfg;2;get
  EXPECT ack;2;wdt_ms=100;deadband_deg=0.5;stream_hz=10;pre_ms=500;post_ms=500
END

CASE cfg-wdt-ms-is-the-host-loss-timeout
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=200
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  ADVANCE 199999
  ADVANCE 1
  EXPECT ev;FAULT;250000;code=0;detail=host_timeout
END


# --------------------------------------------------------- named profiles

CASE moveto-accepts-a-named-profile
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND moveto;4;9.0;present
  EXPECT ack;4
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;TARGET;100000;angle=9.0
  SEND moveto;5;0.0;fast
  EXPECT nak;5;badargs
END


# ----------------------------------------------------------- watch (v1)

CASE watch-outside-released-is-notreleased
  SEND watch;1;pull=5;push=5;timeout=300
  EXPECT nak;1;notreleased
END

# Each outcome, driven by the ANGLE stimulus. The watchdog is widened to 500 ms
# with CFG so the windows below can run without heartbeats; thresholds are
# relative to the angle at RELEASED, pull-positive.

CASE watch-pull-with-hold
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=500
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND brake;5;0
  EXPECT ack;5
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND watch;6;pull=5;push=5;timeout=300;hold=100
  EXPECT ack;6
  ANGLE 6.0
  ADVANCE 99999
  ADVANCE 1
  EXPECT ev;PULL;150000;angle=6.0;torque=
  SEND moveto;7;0.0
  EXPECT ev;TRIAL;150000;outcome=PULL;t_rel=50000;t_touch=;t_move=50000;t_out=150000;a0=0.0;a_peak=6.0;a_end=6.0;tq_peak=;tq_out=;dur_thr=100
  EXPECT ack;7
  ADVANCE 33333
  EXPECT ev;TARGET;183333;angle=0.0
END

# A pull that drops below the threshold before `hold` restarts the hold.
CASE watch-hold-restarts-when-the-pull-is-released
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=500
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND brake;5;0
  EXPECT ack;5
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND watch;6;pull=5;push=5;timeout=300;hold=100
  EXPECT ack;6
  ANGLE 6.0
  ADVANCE 50000
  ANGLE 4.0
  ADVANCE 50000
  ANGLE 6.0
  ADVANCE 99999
  ADVANCE 1
  EXPECT ev;PULL;250000;angle=6.0;torque=
END

CASE watch-push
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=500
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND brake;5;0
  EXPECT ack;5
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND watch;6;pull=5;push=5;timeout=300
  EXPECT ack;6
  ANGLE -6.0
  EXPECT ev;PUSH;50000;angle=-6.0;torque=
  SEND stop;7
  EXPECT ev;TRIAL;50000;outcome=PUSH;t_rel=50000;t_touch=;t_move=50000;t_out=50000;a0=0.0;a_peak=-6.0;a_end=-6.0;tq_peak=;tq_out=;dur_thr=0
  EXPECT ack;7
  SEND status;8
  EXPECT ack;8;state=ARMED;angle=-6.0;xactual=-6.0;torque=;brake=;homed=1;limit=0;faults=0;hv=1;t=50000
END

CASE watch-nomove
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=500
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND brake;5;0
  EXPECT ack;5
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND watch;6;pull=5;push=5;timeout=300
  EXPECT ack;6
  ANGLE 0.2
  ADVANCE 300000
  EXPECT ev;NOMOVE;350000;angle=0.2;torque=
  SEND moveto;7;0.0
  EXPECT ev;TRIAL;350000;outcome=NOMOVE;t_rel=50000;t_touch=;t_move=;t_out=350000;a0=0.0;a_peak=0.2;a_end=0.2;tq_peak=;tq_out=;dur_thr=0
  EXPECT ack;7
  ADVANCE 1111
  EXPECT ev;TARGET;351111;angle=0.0
END

CASE watch-abort
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=500
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND brake;5;0
  EXPECT ack;5
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND watch;6;pull=5;push=5;timeout=300;maxdur=200
  EXPECT ack;6
  ANGLE 2.0
  ADVANCE 200000
  EXPECT ev;ABORT;250000;angle=2.0;torque=
  SEND disarm;7
  EXPECT ev;TRIAL;250000;outcome=ABORT;t_rel=50000;t_touch=;t_move=50000;t_out=250000;a0=0.0;a_peak=2.0;a_end=2.0;tq_peak=;tq_out=;dur_thr=0
  EXPECT ack;7
END

CASE watch-none-when-the-host-leaves-first
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=500
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND brake;5;0
  EXPECT ack;5
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND watch;6;pull=5;push=5;timeout=300
  EXPECT ack;6
  SEND moveto;7;0.0
  EXPECT ev;TRIAL;50000;outcome=NONE;t_rel=50000;t_touch=;t_move=;t_out=;a0=0.0;a_peak=0.0;a_end=0.0;tq_peak=;tq_out=;dur_thr=0
  EXPECT ack;7
  ADVANCE 1
  EXPECT ev;TARGET;50001;angle=0.0
END

# One TRIAL per WATCH: if the host stays RELEASED for a second after the
# outcome the summary comes anyway, and leaving later adds nothing.
CASE trial-comes-after-one-second-if-the-host-stays-released
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=500
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND brake;5;0
  EXPECT ack;5
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND watch;6;pull=5;push=5;timeout=300
  EXPECT ack;6
  ANGLE -6.0
  EXPECT ev;PUSH;50000;angle=-6.0;torque=
  ADVANCE 400000
  SEND ping;7
  EXPECT ack;7
  ADVANCE 400000
  SEND ping;8
  EXPECT ack;8
  ADVANCE 200000
  EXPECT ev;TRIAL;1050000;outcome=PUSH;t_rel=50000;t_touch=;t_move=50000;t_out=50000;a0=0.0;a_peak=-6.0;a_end=-6.0;tq_peak=;tq_out=;dur_thr=0
  SEND stop;9
  EXPECT ack;9
END

# A RELEASED period without a WATCH produces no TRIAL.
CASE no-watch-no-trial
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND brake;4;0
  EXPECT ack;4
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND stop;5
  EXPECT ack;5
END


# ----------------------------------------------------------- fetch (v1)

# The capture is a ring at 1 kHz that runs from RELEASED on, however long the
# trial takes. When the outcome is decided the window freezes post_ms samples
# later: the last pre_ms samples before the outcome sample, the outcome sample
# (k = pre) and the post_ms after it. FETCH is busy until then and returns the
# window in chunks of at most 32 lines. pre reports what the ring holds: here
# RELEASED is 5 ms old at the outcome and pre_ms is 3, so pre is 3.
CASE fetch-returns-the-capture-in-chunks
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=500;pre_ms=3;post_ms=2
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND brake;5;0
  EXPECT ack;5
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND watch;6;pull=5;push=5;timeout=5
  EXPECT ack;6
  SEND fetch;7
  EXPECT nak;7;busy
  ADVANCE 5000
  EXPECT ev;NOMOVE;55000;angle=0.0;torque=
  SEND fetch;8
  EXPECT nak;8;busy
  ADVANCE 2000
  SEND fetch;9
  EXPECT ack;9;n=6;k0=0;t0=52000;dt_us=1000;pre=3
  EXPECT cap;0;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;1;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;2;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;3;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;4;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;5;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;end
  SEND fetch;10;4;2
  EXPECT ack;10;n=2;k0=4;t0=56000;dt_us=1000;pre=3
  EXPECT cap;4;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;5;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;end
  SEND fetch;11;6;2
  EXPECT ack;11;n=0;k0=6;t0=58000;dt_us=1000;pre=3
  EXPECT cap;end
END

# The reason it is a ring: a pull 2.4 s into a 10 s trial is 2401 samples
# after RELEASED, past a 2048-sample linear buffer, and the window still lands
# on it. The host keeps the watchdog fed meanwhile, as a task would.
CASE fetch-window-follows-a-late-outcome-past-the-ring
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=500;pre_ms=2;post_ms=2
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND brake;5;0
  EXPECT ack;5
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND watch;6;pull=5;push=5;timeout=10000;hold=1
  EXPECT ack;6
  ADVANCE 400000
  SEND ping;7
  EXPECT ack;7
  ADVANCE 400000
  SEND ping;8
  EXPECT ack;8
  ADVANCE 400000
  SEND ping;9
  EXPECT ack;9
  ADVANCE 400000
  SEND ping;10
  EXPECT ack;10
  ADVANCE 400000
  SEND ping;11
  EXPECT ack;11
  ADVANCE 400000
  SEND ping;12
  EXPECT ack;12
  ANGLE 6.0
  ADVANCE 1000
  EXPECT ev;PULL;2451000;angle=6.0;torque=
  ADVANCE 2000
  SEND fetch;13
  EXPECT ack;13;n=5;k0=0;t0=2449000;dt_us=1000;pre=2
  EXPECT cap;0;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;1;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;2;6.0;
  EXPECT cap;3;6.0;
  EXPECT cap;4;6.0;
  EXPECT cap;end
END

# The host leaves RELEASED before any outcome: the window freezes at the exit
# with only the samples before it (no outcome sample, so the count equals
# pre), and the history from before the WATCH counts. A new BRAKE restarts
# the ring and the previous window is gone; a RELEASED period without a WATCH
# leaves none.
CASE fetch-after-none-holds-only-the-pre-window
  SEND cfg;1;wdt_ms=500;pre_ms=3;post_ms=3
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND home;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND brake;5;0
  EXPECT ack;5
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;50000;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  ADVANCE 5000
  SEND watch;6;pull=5;push=5;timeout=300
  EXPECT ack;6
  ADVANCE 2000
  SEND moveto;7;0.0
  EXPECT ev;TRIAL;57000;outcome=NONE;t_rel=50000;t_touch=;t_move=;t_out=;a0=0.0;a_peak=0.0;a_end=0.0;tq_peak=;tq_out=;dur_thr=0
  EXPECT ack;7
  SEND fetch;8
  EXPECT ack;8;n=3;k0=0;t0=55000;dt_us=1000;pre=3
  EXPECT cap;0;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;1;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;2;0.0;
  EXPECT cap;end
  ADVANCE 1
  EXPECT ev;TARGET;57001;angle=0.0
  SEND brake;9;0
  EXPECT ack;9
  EXPECT ev;RELEASED;57001;angle=0.0;torque=;brake=
  SEND fetch;10
  EXPECT ack;10;n=0;k0=0;t0=0;dt_us=1000;pre=0
  EXPECT cap;end
END

CASE fetch-before-any-watch-is-empty
  SEND fetch;1
  EXPECT ack;1;n=0;k0=0;t0=0;dt_us=1000;pre=0
  EXPECT cap;end
END


# ---------------------------------------------------------- stream (v1)

CASE stream-is-bounded-and-off-by-default
  SEND stream;1;on;100
  EXPECT nak;1;outofrange
  SEND stream;2;on;50
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 20000
  EXPECT ev;S;20000;angle=0.0;torque=
  ADVANCE 20000
  EXPECT ev;S;40000;angle=0.0;torque=
  SEND stream;3;off
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 100000
END


# --------------------------------------------------- torque (v1.0 boards)

CASE tq-is-badverb-without-torque-hardware
  SEND tq;1;get
  EXPECT nak;1;badverb
END
